newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Colombo stocks end slighly lower on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Colombo stocks end slighly lower on profit-taking.

text.p: Sri Lankan stocks closed slightly lower for the first time in nearly a month, as retail investors sought profits among cheap liquid shares, brokers said.
The all share index closed 1.37 points lower at 591.83 after a slow and steady rise from 558.10 points on September 10, mainly on buying by retail investors of selected shares, they said.
"Retail buying was instrumental in taking the market up. And now that the index is above 590 points they are returning to take profit," said Sriyan Gurusinghe of Bartleet Mallory Stockbrokers.
Ceylon Tobacco, Distilleries and Vanik fell 25 cents each to 28.50 rupees, 6.25 and 13.
Small retailers, who are normally happy with profits of three to four percent, have been taking seven to eight percent among liquid cheap stocks, Gurusinghe said.
Turnover was a thin 12.9 million rupees.

Brokers said turnover was low due to an absence of foreign investors. "Foreign interest is still there, but you have to be able to source stock in bulk to get them in," said a trader at Asia Securities.
